results.title: Data Infrastructure as Code: Automating the Full Data Platform Lifecycle
results.content: # Data Infrastructure as Code: Automating the Full Data Platform Lifecycle. While most engineers are familiar with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for provisioning cloud resources, leading organizations are now taking this concept further by implementing "Data Infrastructure as Code" – a comprehensive approach that automates the entire data platform lifecycle. It encompasses the automation of schema management, compute resources, access controls, data quality rules, observability, and every other aspect of a modern data platform. Modern data teams treat database schemas as versioned artifacts that evolve through controlled processes rather than ad-hoc changes:. * Automated review processes: CI/CD pipelines that validate schema changes before deployment. This approach allows teams to manage database schemas with the same discipline applied to application code, including peer reviews, automated testing, and versioned releases. Let's explore how different organizations have implemented comprehensive Data Infrastructure as Code:. 2. Compatibility rules as code: Automated validation of schema changes against compatibility policies. 4. Phased deployment orchestration: Automated coordination of schema changes across systems. A healthcare organization implemented an automated approach to data access:. * Immuta and Privacera: Automated data access governance. ### Benefits of the Data Infrastructure as Code Approach. For organizations looking to implement Data Infrastructure as Code, here's a practical roadmap:. Implement basic CI/CD for infrastructure: Automated testing and deployment of infrastructure changes. ### Phase 2: Schema and Data Pipeline Automation (2-4 months). 2. Set up automated testing for schema changes: Validate changes before deployment. 3. Establish data quality rules as code: Define and automate data quality checks. 2. Implement approval workflows: Automate the access request process. The most successful data organizations are those that have embraced comprehensive automation through Data Infrastructure as Code. Rather than treating infrastructure, schemas, and policies as separate concerns managed through different processes, Data Infrastructure as Code brings them together into a cohesive, automated system. Organizations that adopt comprehensive automation will pull ahead, delivering faster, more reliable data capabilities while maintaining robust governance and optimizing resources. The question for data leaders is no longer whether to automate, but how quickly and comprehensively they can implement Data Infrastructure as Code to transform their data platforms. How far along is your organization in automating your data platform?

results.title: How to Make Your Data Analysis Transparent and Reproducible
results.content: To make data analysis more transparent and reproducible, \* it is important to clearly define the research question, \* document the code, \* use open-source tools, \* share the data, create a reproducibility package, \* use literate programming, and \* perform sensitivity analyses These best practices and tools help to ensure that the analysis is transparent, reproducible, and reliable. 1) Document process comprehensively 2) Utilize Git for version control & collaboration 3) Organize code into modules with meaningful names 4) Manage dependencies and specify software versions 5) Share raw and processed data using standard formats 6) Use tools like Jupyter notebooks for executable documentation 7) Automate workflows to minimize manual errors 8) Perform sensitivity analysis to test robustness 9) Engage peers for code reviews 10) Generate versioned reports capturing code, visualisation & results 11) Apply open-source licenses to define usage terms 12) Offer supplementary materials for research publications 13) Implement continuous integration for ongoing projects 14) Share openly & seek community feedback for improvements.

results.title: A Modular Approach to Reproducible Research - Data & Design Lab
results.content: This blog covers essential modules for ensuring reproducibility: **package and environment management**, **reproducible data pipelines**, **version control for code, reports, and data**, **reproducible output**, and the **advantages of plain text formats**. A **reproducible data pipeline** ensures that given the same raw data and the same processing steps, the outputs will be the same. ### Example: Data Pipeline with Snakemake # Example rule in Snakemake for processing data "python process_data.py {input} {output}" By defining each step of the data processing in a reproducible pipeline, researchers can ensure consistent results across multiple runs. Tools like **Git** for code and documents, and **Data Version Control (DVC)** for large datasets, help ensure that each aspect of your research can be traced and reproduced at any point in time. ### Example: Version Control for Code with Git # Initialize a Git repository # Add your code, environment, and report files git add script.py environment.yml report.tex # Commit your changes git commit -m "Initial commit with code, environment, and report" ### Data Version Control with DVC: When working with large datasets, DVC can help version your data and link it to specific versions of your code. ### Example: Version Control for Data with DVC # Initialize DVC in your project # Track a large dataset dvc add data/raw_data.csv # Add the data version to Git git add data/raw_data.csv.dvc git commit -m "Add versioned data" This setup ensures that both code and data can be versioned together, so changes in data are linked to specific code versions. 4. Reproducible Output: Results and Charts With the environment and data pipeline set up, the next focus is ensuring that the research output — whether it’s results, figures, or charts — is consistent. By adopting a modular approach to reproducible research, you can ensure that every aspect of your work—environment, data pipeline, code, results, and reports—can be replicated by others. Starting with environment management, followed by reproducible data pipelines, and finally tracking everything with version control, researchers can create transparent and robust workflows. Using plain text formats like `.py`, LaTeX, and Typst enhances version control and ensures that code, data, and documents remain lightweight and version-traceable.

results.title: Datasets and Computer Vision - Valohai
results.content: The lack of a unified process for linking the data sources with deep learning projects means no communication between the teams, no versioning of changes, and a situation where anything can potentially break everything. Valohai creates a managed layer between data and projects, allowing communication and versioning over time. ### Enter Valohai Datasets. A new core concept for creating a unified process is the **Valohai dataset**. It creates a common ground for managing, versioning, and communicating unstructured data. Let's look deeper into how Valohai datasets are created and what they can do for you. First way to create Valohai datasets is by **adopting** them. Another way to create Valohai datasets is by **transforming** existing datasets into new ones. Different dataset transformations and training steps can be combined into a reproducible Valohai pipeline. Therefore everything in Valohai is versioned and traceable. Versioning and managing big unstructured data for machine vision is not a solved problem. No obvious standard for versioning and managing big unstructured data in a machine vision project exists. ### Valohai Dataset. Valohai datasets are the versioning standard that sits comfortably among the others. Valohai **dataset:version** is to unstructured data what **repository:commit** is for code, and what **image:tag** is for dependencies. Valohai datasets are versioned and managed with the same ethos as code and dependencies, and they are trackable and reproducible similarly, too. Now that we have solved dataset versioning, the data, code, and dependencies can come together in a fully reproducible and trackable ML experiment. We introduce one final name & version pair, the **project:execution** in Valohai. Valohai datasets are not physical but virtual, which means that the data is never duplicated. The datasets are references to the customer's data storage, which Valohai manages externally. The dataset version is designed to be immutable to ensure full reproducibility. A transformation step should always create a new version of the dataset instead of modifying existing files directly within the data storage. As a pioneer-friendly platform, Valohai still lets customers manually modify the data at their own risk. * Valohai datasets make implementing a unified process around data effortless through automatic versioning, sharing, and clear linkage between steps and datasets.
